exposure: mode of delivery (elective vs. emergency cesarean section)
outcome: admission to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: 588 women undergoing cesarean section at a tertiary maternity hospital in Rabat, Morocco
finding: Fetal complications were higher in emergency cesarean sections compared to elective cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean section was associated with younger mothers, maternal illiteracy, primiparity, insufficient prenatal care, referral from other institutions, cesarean section performed under general anesthesia, lower birth weight, neonatal morbidity, early mortality, and admission to the neonatal intensive care unit.
birth_weight: Lower birth weight was associated with emergency cesarean section.
